verses.text: He said to me, "Son of man, eat what is in front of you. Eat this scroll, and then go and speak to the people of Israel."
So I opened my mouth, and he gave me the scroll to eat.
He said to me, "Son of man, eat this scroll I am giving you and fill your stomach with it." So I ate it, and it tasted as sweet as honey in my mouth.
Then he said to me, "Son of man, go to the people of Israel and speak my words to them.
I am not sending you to a people with a strange and difficult language, but to the people of Israel.
I am not sending you to many nations with strange and difficult languages, whose words you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would surely listen to you.
But the people of Israel will not listen to you, because they are not willing to listen to me. All the people of Israel are stubborn and hard-hearted.
But look, I have made you as unyielding and hard-headed as they are.
I have made your forehead like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or frightened by their looks, even though they are a rebellious people."
Then he said to me, "Son of man, listen carefully to all the words I speak to you, and take them to heart.
Go to your people who are in exile and speak to them. Tell them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says,' whether they listen or refuse to listen."
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and behind me I heard a loud rumbling sound: "Praise the glory of the LORD from his place!"
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, a loud rumbling sound.
The Spirit lifted me up and took me away. I went in bitterness and anger, and the LORD's power was strong on me.
I came to the exiles who lived at Tel Abib by the Kebar River. I sat among them for seven days, overwhelmed.
At the end of the seven days, the LORD's message came to me:
"Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel. Whenever you hear a message from my mouth, warn them for me.

If I say to a wicked person, 'You will surely die,' and you do not warn them or speak out to turn them from their wicked ways to save their life, that wicked person will die for their sin. But I will hold you responsible for their death.
But if you warn the wicked person and they do not turn from their wickedness or their wicked ways, they will die for their sin, but you will have saved yourself.

And if a righteous person turns from doing right and does evil, and I put a stumbling block in front of them, they will die. Since you did not warn them, they will die for their sin. The right things they did will not be remembered, and I will hold you responsible for their death.
But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and they do not sin, they will surely live because they listened to the warning. And you will have saved yourself."
The LORD's power came on me there, and he said to me, "Get up and go out to the plain, and I will speak to you there."
So I got up and went out to the plain. And there was the glory of the LORD, just like the glory I had seen by the Kebar River. I fell face down on the ground.
Then the Spirit came into me and stood me on my feet. He spoke to me and said, "Go and lock yourself inside your house.
And you, son of man, they will tie you up with ropes, so that you cannot go out among the people.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you cannot speak or correct them, because they are a rebellious people.

But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' Whoever will listen, let them listen. Whoever refuses, let them refuse, for they are a rebellious people."
